sections.h2: Where is Dubuque County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Dubuque County is in eastern Iowa, where the state meets Illinois and Wisconsin, and the Mississippi River forms its northeastern edge. The county seat and largest city is Dubuque. The 2020 census counted 99,266 residents, which made it the ninth most populous county in Iowa.

The county covers about 616 square miles. The east is hilly and wooded, part of the Driftless Area that glaciers skipped, while the west is mostly rolling farmland. Beyond Dubuque, the biggest communities in 2020 were Asbury (5,943 people), Dyersville (4,477), Cascade (2,386), Epworth (2,023), Peosta (1,908) and Farley (1,766).

The county was founded on October 1, 1834 and takes its name from Julien Dubuque, a French Canadian trader. The city of Dubuque was chartered a year earlier and is counted as the oldest city in Iowa. A house in a river bluff neighborhood and a house on a farm near Cascade can both be sold here, but they are taxed and assessed through the same county machinery, which is what this guide covers.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Dubuque County?
sections.html:
The Dubuque County Treasurer collects property tax, and the assessor's office for your parcel sets the value. The City of Dubuque states on its own site that it does not bill or collect property taxes. The county assesses and collects them, then passes the city's share along each month.

  • Treasurer: Michael Clasen, County Court House, 720 Central Avenue, Dubuque, IA 52001. The city's page lists office hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.
  • Courthouse main line: 563-589-1300, mailing address PO Box 5001, Dubuque, IA 52004-5001.
  • Appointments: the county website says the treasurer's office takes appointments that can be booked online to skip the line.
  • Property search: the county links a Beacon property records lookup from its home page.

Dubuque also has a city assessor. A 2020 presentation to the city council was given by Troy Patzner as Dubuque City Assessor, so a parcel inside city limits may be valued by that office rather than the county's. If you are unsure, call the courthouse and give the parcel number.

sections.h2: When are Dubuque County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Iowa property tax is paid in two halves, and the statewide calendar applies to Dubuque County. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with a grace period to the end of each month.

  • Statements go out in August after the county auditor certifies the levy.
  • September 30 is the first-half deadline, and March 31 is the second-half deadline. If either date lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day.
  • Unpaid first-half tax is delinquent in October and unpaid second-half tax in April.
  • Interest on a delinquent installment runs 1.5 percent per month, with a one dollar minimum.

Iowa taxes run a year behind. The September and March payments cover the fiscal year that ended the previous June 30. That matters if you sell: you can owe tax for a period when the house was still yours even if the buyer takes over before the bill arrives.

A missing statement does not remove late charges. The state's treasurers' association says it is the owner's job to make sure a bill is received and paid, and you can pay with just the parcel number.

sections.h2: How does the Dubuque County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Dubuque County holds a yearly online tax sale for parcels with unpaid tax, usually on the third Monday of June. The 2026 sale was set for Monday, June 15, 2026, with bidding open from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. at iowataxauction.com. Bidders had to register by June 11.

The scale is worth seeing. The county's 2025 publication notice, for a June 16, 2025 sale, listed roughly 450 real estate parcels and about 130 mobile homes. Real estate amounts on that list ran from $6 to $104,077, including penalty and costs.

  • Redemption interest is 2 percent per month on the sale amount, and any part of a month counts as a full month.
  • On a regular sale, a 90-day notice of right of redemption may be issued after one year and nine months from the sale date.
  • On a public bidder sale, the 90-day notice may go out nine months after the sale.
  • A redemption only counts if the treasurer receives it before close of business on the 90th day after service is complete.

A property marked with an asterisk in the notice has been advertised for two years without a sale. If no private bid arrives, the county itself bids the amount due. Anyone holding such a parcel and thinking of selling should talk to the treasurer before the next June sale.

sections.h2: How are Dubuque homes valued, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
Iowa assessors value residential property at 100 percent of market value, then a state rollback percentage cuts that to a taxable value. Dubuque's own assessor explained the method in 2020: sales of similar homes, replacement cost less depreciation, and for rentals an income approach.

Real property is reassessed every two years, in odd-numbered years. The Department of Revenue checks assessments against actual sales, and if a class falls outside a 95 to 105 percent ratio band it can order an adjustment. In Dubuque's 2019 cycle the residential rollback was 55.0743 percent. Rollbacks change every year, and a 2025 example from the Iowa Taxpayers Research foundation used 44.5345 percent for residential property. Statewide taxable growth for existing homes is capped at 3 percent.

To contest a value, you file a written protest with the local Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. Iowa Code 441.37 allows five grounds:

  • the assessment is not equitable compared with similar property;
  • it is above the value the law allows;
  • the property is misclassified or should be exempt;
  • there is an error in the assessment;
  • there was fraud or misconduct, which must be stated specifically.

A hearing can be requested in writing when you file. The board must send a written decision with its reasons. If you disagree, the next step is the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court, and the PAAB can be reached at 515-725-0338.

sections.h2: What does the Dubuque economy mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Dubuque's employer base is broad, which keeps a steady pool of local buyers and renters. The city's largest employers include John Deere (about 2,600 people), the Dubuque Community School District (about 1,957), MercyOne Dubuque Medical Center (about 1,410) and Medical Associates (about 1,061). Finley Hospital, Andersen Windows and Doors, Sedgwick Claims Management Services and Medline Industries are also major names.

Manufacturing was the base until the 1980s farm crisis, when unemployment in the county hit 23 percent in one month of 1982. The economy has since added health care, finance, education and tourism, and the city draws more than 2 million visitors a year to the Port of Dubuque and its riverfront.

Five colleges are in the city: Loras, Clarke, the University of Dubuque, Emmaus University and a Northeast Iowa Community College campus presence, with the largest NICC campus in nearby Peosta. Anyone selling near a campus or in the older parts of the city should expect buyers to compare the house with its neighbors on age and condition.

sections.h2: What property conditions affect a Dubuque County sale?
sections.html:
Hills, river flooding and age are the three physical issues buyers ask about first. The city sits among bluffs in the Driftless Area, so slope matters when a buyer looks at a lot. Lower areas by the river and creeks carry flood risk, and the city has worked on the North End by opening up parts of Bee Branch Creek in 2015 and 2016. Flash flooding in places such as Valley View is still being dealt with.

Dubuque's neighborhoods have different building eras. The downtown area includes the Fenelon Place Residential Historic District, the North End grew with German settlers, the South End is historically Irish American, and the West End grew after World War II. A 2020 housing count found 27,174 units in the city, with a 1.5 percent homeowner vacancy rate.

Older houses in any of these areas often need roofs, wiring, foundation work or sewer line repairs before a traditional buyer's inspector signs off. A cash sale as-is avoids that repair list, though you should still confirm taxes and any special assessments with the treasurer first.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when you sell a Dubuque County house?
sections.html:
Taxes are normally prorated on the closing statement, with the buyer credited for the seller's share or the seller paying the treasurer directly. The state's treasurers' site adds that a seller closing between July 1 and December 31 owes the September installment, and a seller closing between January 1 and June 30 owes the March installment.

  • Delinquent tax and tax sale amounts must be paid in full before a clean transfer.
  • Every deed that conveys Iowa real estate for more than $500 carries state transfer tax of 80 cents per $500 or fraction above $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1).
  • A declaration of value, signed by a buyer or seller, goes to the county recorder with the deed. The recorder sends it to the assessor, who keeps it for three years.

Because the assessor receives those declarations, your sale price can become evidence in later valuation work. That is one reason to keep the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Dubuque County?
faqs.a: You pay the Dubuque County Treasurer at the courthouse, 720 Central Avenue in Dubuque, or by calling the courthouse for current payment options. The City of Dubuque does not collect property tax.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the September 30 payment in Dubuque County?
faqs.a: The first half becomes delinquent in October and interest of 1.5 percent per month is added, with a one dollar minimum. If it stays unpaid, the parcel can be listed for the June tax sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dubuque County house that is in the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes, but the delinquent tax, penalty and costs have to be paid, usually from the sale proceeds at closing. Once a certificate is sold, redemption also carries 2 percent interest per month on the sale amount.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Dubuque County assessment?
faqs.a: Written protests go to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. Outside that window, only clerical or mathematical errors can be corrected.
